### Executive Summary
Citrix has confirmed active, in-the-wild exploitation of zero-day Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerabilities affecting its NetScaler platform. The ongoing attack campaign targets unpatched NetScaler instances, presenting a critical risk to enterprise environments relying on these appliances for access control and networking.

Detailed metrics regarding the full extent of the targeting and the specific threat actors involved are currently not yet confirmed. Organizations utilizing NetScaler products should immediately treat these devices as high-priority critical assets requiring heightened monitoring.

### Technical Impact & Root Cause
The identified vulnerabilities permit unauthorized Remote Code Execution (RCE) on impacted Citrix NetScaler devices. If successfully exploited, an attacker could potentially execute arbitrary code, bypass security boundaries, and establish unauthorized access within the enterprise network perimeter.

The specific underlying software bugs, affected NetScaler firmware versions, and precise technical root causes have not yet been detailed in the available report. Further investigation is required to analyze the exact mechanism used to achieve remote code execution.

### Mitigation & IOCs
Concrete vendor mitigations, technical workarounds, and official patch updates have not yet been confirmed in the initial reporting. Network administrators should monitor official Citrix security advisories closely for emergency patches and restrict administrative access to NetScaler appliances from untrusted networks.
